name: NiSource Inc.
moat_justification: Exclusive regulated service territories and essential service make the franchise durable, but NiSource owns no pricing power beyond what commissions grant, allowed ROE is under active scrutiny in Indiana, and the equity story depends on regulators continuing to let a very large capex program into rate base.
fragility_flags: STALE_FY: latest fiscal year ended 9 months ago — check TTM/quarterly OE and consider --base-oe-ps override
NI_OCF_DIVERGENCE: net income and operating cash flow differ by >40% in 2023, 2025 — find the one-off (tax deposits, impairments, WC swings) before trusting the OE base
SECTOR_MODEL_MISMATCH: Utilities sector — OE/capex DCF fits utilities names poorly; grade confidence low
one_liner: Regulated utility monopoly, moat 5/10 — conservative owner's earnings are negative in all of the last 5 fiscal years (capex for rate-base and data-center growth far exceeds OCF), so the OE DCF returns Tier F at $41.25 with no hurdle-clearing price on this method; verdict is method-bound, confidence low.
moat_for: Exclusive regulated monopoly territories (Columbia Gas, NIPSCO) — customers cannot switch providers
Essential gas and electric service with inelastic demand
Rate-base growth engine — $28.6B 2026–2030 plan guided to 9%–11% rate-base growth, Amazon/Alphabet data-center agreements approved in Indiana
Long-lived infrastructure franchise with tracker/modernization cost recovery
moat_against: Returns capped by regulators — no pricing power beyond rate cases and trackers
Indiana ROE and tracker proceedings under scrutiny (BMO cut target $49 to $45 on 2026-09-28 citing regulatory clarity)
Perpetual external financing — ~$400M–$600M/yr planned equity issuance dilutes (share count CAGR +2.34%/yr); heavy debt load makes earnings rate-sensitive
GenCo data-center build adds large-load, counterparty and execution risk outside the traditional regulated model
